Break a natural number into its prime factors, smallest first.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/prime-factors) (MIT). Listed under [Numbers & Math](/examples/?subject=numbers-and-math).

```nomi-run
// FILE: prime_factors.nomi
//# The prime factors of a number.

/// The prime factors of `value`, smallest first, each repeated as often as it
/// divides `value`.
pub fn factors(value: Int) -> List<Int> {
    factors_from(value, 2)
}

fn factors_from(n: Int, divisor: Int) -> List<Int> {
    if n == 1 {
        []
    } else if divisor * divisor > n {
        [n]
    } else if n % divisor == 0 {
        [divisor, ..factors_from(n / divisor, divisor)]
    } else {
        factors_from(n, divisor + 1)
    }
}

// FILE: prime_factors_test.nomi
import prime_factors

test "factors" {
    cases = [
        #("no factors", 1, []),
        #("prime number", 2, [2]),
        #("another prime number", 3, [3]),
        #("square of a prime", 9, [3, 3]),
        #("product of first prime", 4, [2, 2]),
        #("cube of a prime", 8, [2, 2, 2]),
        #("product of second prime", 27, [3, 3, 3]),
        #("product of third prime", 625, [5, 5, 5, 5]),
        #("product of first and second prime", 6, [2, 3]),
        #("product of primes and non-primes", 12, [2, 2, 3]),
        #("product of primes", 901255, [5, 17, 23, 461]),
        #("factors include a large prime", 93819012551, [11, 9539, 894119]),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, value, expected), description {
        assert prime_factors.factors(value) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Trial division by recursion: `factors_from(n, divisor)` either conses a factor onto the rest (`[divisor, ..factors_from(n / divisor, divisor)]`) or moves to the next divisor in tail position. The non-tail call happens once per factor, so the depth is at most 63.
- It stops as soon as `divisor * divisor > n`, which keeps the large-prime case (93819012551) to about 9,500 steps.
- An `if`/`else if` chain rather than `case { cond -> ... }`; four conditions in order read the same either way.
- One `subtests` table for all 12 cases.
